comment: A call to a function the CSS grammar does not know — `d(--accent)`, a slip for `var(`. The CSS grammar pairs the brackets only of the functions it knows, so the `)` closing an unknown one was the first one left, and it ended the BLOCK: the `(` had no partner, and an editor painted it red with no message. `R:` puts this AFTER the CSS grammar's own patterns, so a function it knows keeps its own colour and only an unknown one is read here. The checker says what is wrong with the name — `unknown-function`.
